LHX.sentence: L3Harris slipped a touch, and the real thing to watch isn't the stock price but their profit margins, which are running below their usual level and have room to recover as the smallest of the big defense contractors.

ASML.sentence: ASML pulled back a little, but nothing's wrong — they're still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, and demand for those keeps coming.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — the world's biggest industrial gas supplier keeps chugging along, and unusually it's now priced no richer than its main rival despite being the better-run operator.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft had a strong week and has badly outrun the rest of the AI pack lately, so it's become the crowded favorite everyone already owns — the cloud-and-AI story keeps grinding along nicely, it's just no longer a bargain.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is steady, and there's a hopeful sign underneath — biotech funding is thawing again, which usually shows up in their lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is calm — the Canadian pipeline toll-road business keeps paying a hefty dividend that's well above what you'd get lending to the government.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow had a good week — big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow-automation and AI-assistant tools, and after a pullback the price is back to a more reasonable level for how fast it's growing.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore is holding steady, with a generous dividend backed by its copper and other mines plus its huge commodity-trading arm, and no sign the metals cycle has peaked.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta eased slightly, but the number that matters — the price it gets per ton of crushed stone — is still climbing for the fourth quarter running, so the business remains as solid as ever even though the headline earnings look distorted by a one-off asset swap.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is uneventful — this Latin American Coke bottler mostly rides on the Mexican peso, and the peso has been stable, so there's no drama here.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is quiet, but comfortably so — oil is fetching far more than it costs them to pump it from their deepwater fields, which easily funds the big dividend this Brazilian oil company is known for.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant that moves goods around the world on ships, is trading below what its fleet is actually worth — historically a decent point to own it in the shipping cycle.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped a hair, but people keep tapping their cards more and more, and it's unusually priced barely above rival Visa despite growing a bit faster.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company is down sharply from its high even though it expects to do meaningfully more operations next year — a gap between fear and the actual business, since most of its money comes from supplies used in each surgery.
